summary: The passage describes a monetary transmission mechanism where a 525-basis-point tightening cycle compressed aggregate demand, raising unemployment from 3.4% to 4.1%, which in turn reduced wage-cost pressures that had been feeding sticky services-ex-housing inflation. Despite headline PCE inflation decelerating to 2.4%, persistent wage-sensitive service price stickiness and geopolitical energy volatility create upside risks. The Committee balanced these concerns against progress on inflation, authorizing a 25-basis-point rate cut while warning that premature easing could reignite inflation expectations. The decision reflects data-dependent policy guided by labor market slack, core goods disinflation, and proximity to the 2% inflation target.
